rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruined people are told to stop fleeing and return to former comforts or positions, so they can face questioning and humiliation.
rows.anchor: لا تركضوا وارجعوا لعلكم تسئلون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The command may be spoken by angels or believers, addressed to people who deserve it, or spoken by God for angels to hear and benefit from.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري: يحتمل أن يكون يعني القائل بعض الملائكة،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Returning means resuming luxurious life, sitting in former assemblies, receiving servants’ orders and public consultation, or hosting petitioners for alms.
rows.anchor: وارجعوا إلى ما أترفتم فيه من العيش الرافه والحال الناعمة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The taunt fits either former generosity performed for praise or miserliness; the command compounds mockery and rebuke.
rows.anchor: إما لأنهم كانوا أسخياء ينفقون أموالهم رياء الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling for woe is figurative, as if the condemned summon woe to arrive.
rows.anchor: ونداء الويل هو على سبيل المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wrongdoing means associating partners with God, denying messengers, and bringing themselves to ruin.
rows.anchor: والظلم هنا الإشراك وتكذيب الرسل وإيقاع أنفسهم في الهلاك

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The people kept repeating their cry, but it did not help them, like faith that comes only upon seeing punishment.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: فما زالوا يكررون تلك الكلمة فلم تنفعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun دعوى is a verbal noun from دعا; the cries of woe are phrased as a call.
rows.anchor: والدعوى مصدر دعا يقال: دعا دعوى ودعوة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Zajjaj, followed by al-Hawfi, al-Zamakhshari, and Abu al-Baqa, permits either تلك as subject and دعواهم as predicate or the reverse.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذهب إليه هؤلاء قاله الزجاج قبلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan follows later grammarians: in an ambiguous كان clause, the first noun remains its subject, so تلك is اسم زالت and دعواهم its predicate.
rows.anchor: على ما قرره جمهور الأصحاب يتعين أن يكون تلك اسم زالت ودعواهم الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punished townspeople were left like harvested crops: dead, lifeless, and like a fire after it goes out; حصيدا is a second object.
rows.anchor: بالعذاب تركوا كالحصيد خامدين أي موتى دون أرواح

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi treats خامدين as an adjective of حصيدا understood collectively as harvested people, or as a circumstantial clause referring to them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل خامدين حالا من الهاء والميم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains جعلناهم like making people ashes: جعل takes the former subject plus two predicate complements as objects.
rows.anchor: جعلناهم مثل الحصيد شبههم في استئصالهم واصطلامهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Three apparent objects are justified because the last two jointly express being both crop-like and extinguished; خامدين coordinates with the likeness, not حصيد.
rows.anchor: والخمود عطف على المماثلة لا على الحصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s destruction of unjust towns is just recompense; the upper and lower worlds were made for religious outcomes and innumerable worldly benefits, not play.
rows.anchor: أتبع ذلك بما يدل على أنه فعل ذلك عدلا منه ومجازاة

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani defines play as an ignorant act attractive at first but lacking permanence; creation instead enables reward, punishment, and proof of divine unity and power.
rows.anchor: اللعب فعل يدعو إليه الجهل يروق أوله ولا ثبات له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s argument is linked to statements that heaven, earth, and what lies between them were not created vainly or without truth.
rows.anchor: كقوله وما خلقنا السماء والأرض وما بينهما باطلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لهو originally means what desire quickly seeks and whim prompts; it can be a euphemism for sexual intercourse.
rows.anchor: أصل اللهو ما تسرع إليه الشهوة ويدعو إليه الهوى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi interpret the amusement God would take as a child; al-Zajjaj says this is the Hadrami use.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس والسدي هو الولد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says لهو means child in the dialect of Hadramawt.
rows.anchor: هو الولد بلغة حضر موت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also reads the amusement as play, and says the verse answers those who claim God has a child.
rows.anchor: وعنه أن اللهو هنا اللعب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says wisdom prevents God from taking play; His ability is affirmed only if play is meant, since a child or wife is impossible and not within the scope of power.
rows.anchor: ولا يجيء هذا إلا على قول من قال: اللهو هو اللعب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent syntax makes أن conditional, with its omitted result supplied by the following لو clause; God would do this only if He were one who did it.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن أن هنا شرطية وجواب الشرط محذوف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Jurayj read أن as a negation: God would not do this.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: وقتادة وجريج أن نافية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the truth hurled at falsehood as the Qur’an and falsehood as Satan; he says every Qur’anic use of falsehood means Satan.
rows.anchor: وهو الشيطان قاله مجاهد، وقال كل ما في القرآن من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes truth as proof that defeats falsehood, including their false descriptions of God as having a child.
rows.anchor: بالحجة على الباطل وهو شبههم ووصفهم الله بغير صفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A broader interpretation makes truth Qur’an, messengerhood, and law, and falsehood the corresponding general opposite.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الحق عام في القرآن والرسالة والشرع، والباطل أيضا عام كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بل shifts away from the idea of play: truth demolishes falsehood, vividly likened to a hard object striking and killing a hollow body.
rows.anchor: استعار لذلك القذف والدمغ تصويرا لإبطاله وإهداره ومحقه

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads فيدمغه with an accusative final غ; al-Zamakhshari calls this weak and compares it with a poetic line ending فأستريحا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر فيدمغه بنصب الغين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: A further reading has a ḍamma on the mīm in فيدمغه.
rows.anchor: وقرىء فيدمغه بضم الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat of woe addresses disbelievers for attributing a consort, child, and other impossible qualities to God.
rows.anchor: أي الخزي والهم مما تصفون أي تصفونه مما لا يليق به تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view addresses those who deny messengers and call the Qur’an magic or confused dreams; Abu Hayyan rejects as remote the proposed shift from third-person to direct address.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أنه التفات من ضمير الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as being with God are angels; عنده expresses honor and rank, not physical location, since God is beyond place.
rows.anchor: وعند هنا لا يراد بها ظرف المكان لأنه تعالى منزه عن المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Syntactically, ومن عنده may coordinate with من, with لا يستكبرون as a circumstantial clause or new statement, or it may begin a new subject clause.
rows.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون ومن عنده مبتدأ وخبره لا يستكبرون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows وله من في السماوات والأرض to balance the warning addressed to the condemned.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون معادلا لقوله ولكم الويل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that interpreting amusement as a woman is Yemeni usage and rebuts the claim that God has a wife.
rows.anchor: اللهو هنا المرأة. وقال قتادة: هذا في لغة أهل اليمن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من لدنا can mean “from God” in a hidden way, since the alleged deficiency should be concealed.
rows.anchor: ومعنى من لدنا من عندنا بحيث لا يطلع عليه أحد لأنه نقص فستره أولى

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi understands من لدنا as from heaven rather than earth.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: من السماء لا من الأرض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views identify the hidden gift as houris or as an act of divine power.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الحور العين. وقيل: من جهة قدرتنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the gift would be angels rather than humans, refuting claims concerning Christ and Ezra.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من الملائكة لا من الإنس ردا لولادة المسيح وعزيز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are honored and placed, by way of illustration, like trusted courtiers near a king, which explains their distinction and merit.
rows.anchor: مكرمون منزلون لكرامتهم على الله منزلة المقربين عند الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حسر and استحسر describe a camel becoming exhausted; a cited line about exhausted camels supplies lexical evidence.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: بها جيف الحسرى فأما عظامها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the intensive استحسار indicates that their worship could cause the greatest exhaustion, yet they remain devoted to its demanding acts.
rows.anchor: في الاستحسار بيان أن ما هم فيه يوجب غاية الحسور وأقصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All Muslims agree that the angels are meant by يسبحون, and the verse portrays their glorification as continuous.
rows.anchor: يسبحون هم الملائكة بإجماع الأمة وصفهم بتسبيح دائم

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka‘b says God made glorification for angels like breathing and blinking for humans, so it continues without weariness.
rows.anchor: جعل الله لهم التسبيح كالنفس وطرف العين للبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says the sky groans, rightly so: no space the size of a handspan lacks an angel prostrating or standing; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: إني لأسمع أطيط السماء وحق لها أن تئط

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari objects that idolaters did not claim their gods could resurrect, although they acknowledged God as creator and denied resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: كيف أنكر عليهم اتخاذ آلهة تنشر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He answers that claiming divinity entails claiming the ability to create, including to resurrect; this taunts their inconsistency about what they deem possible for God.
rows.anchor: ولكنهم بادعائهم الإلهية يلزمهم أن يدعوا لها الإنشاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: من الأرض may mark idols worshiped on earth, without assigning God a heavenly location; the slave-girl report is understood as rejecting earthly idols, not locating God.
rows.anchor: الإيذان بأنها الأصنام التي تعبد في الأرض لا أن الآلهة أرضية وسماوية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Alternatively, the idols are from earth in material, since they are carved from stone or made from earthly substances.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد آلهة من جنس الأرض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The pronoun هم stresses exclusivity: these idols alone would be the ones able to create.
rows.anchor: إفادة معنى الخصوصية كأنه قيل أم اتخذوا آلهة لا تقدر على الإنشاء إلا هم وحدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اتخذوا may mean that they fashioned images, or that they made the gods into idols from earthly material; the latter use can also mean appointing or choosing.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المعنى فيها صنعوا وصوروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read ينشرون from أنشر, meaning revive; Qutrub glosses it as create, while Hasan and Mujahid read نشر, another transitive form that can also be intransitive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ينشرون مضارع أنشر ومعناه يحيون

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub explains ينشرون as creating, like the Qur’anic contrast between one who creates and one who does not.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب: معناه يخلقون كقوله أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual pronoun in فيهما refers to heaven and earth as a metonym for the whole world.
rows.anchor: والضمير في فيهما عائد على السماء والأرض وهما كناية عن العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line cited from Sibawayh shows that Arabic can use إلا adjectivally to mean “other than.”
rows.anchor: وكل أخ مفارقه أخوه ... لعمر أبيك إلا الفرقدان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari rejects raising الله as an appositive after إلا because لو introduces a formally affirmative clause, unlike a negative context where replacement is licensed.
rows.anchor: لأن لو بمنزلة إن في أن الكلام معه موجب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: If multiple gods governed heaven and earth, they would be corrupted; the proof establishes one governor and that this one is God alone.
rows.anchor: وجوب أن لا يكون مدبرهما إلا واحدا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari argues that multiple kings cause disorder through rivalry, illustrated by Abd al-Malik’s remark that two stallions cannot share a herd.
rows.anchor: لا يجتمع فحلان في شول

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The proof also draws on the theologians’ mutual-obstruction argument and on created effects needing one distinct essence and attributes to stabilize them.
rows.anchor: هذه الأفعال محتاجة إلى تلك الذات المتميزة بتلك الصفات

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya argues that conflicting wills cannot both govern an event; if only one succeeds, the other is incapable and therefore not divine.
rows.anchor: إذا تمت الواحدة كان صاحب الأخرى عاجزا وهذا ليس بإله

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya adds that one event cannot be produced by two powers; the second would contribute nothing to it.
rows.anchor: فمحال أن تتعلق به قدرتان

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi argues that two necessary beings would share existence yet differ; each would then be composite and dependent, so only one necessary being exists and the world is created.
rows.anchor: فإذا واجب الوجود ليس إلا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument by reductio says that supposing two necessary beings would leave no necessary being and thus no possible world.
rows.anchor: يلزم من فرض موجودين واجبين أن لا يكون شيء منهما واجبا

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa rejects apposition because it would make the conditional mean that God alone among the gods was present, rather than that there is no god but Him.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون بدلا لأن المعنى يصير إلى قولك لو كان فيهما

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: He rejects exception parsing for two reasons: it yields the false sense that God’s presence prevents cosmic corruption, and the indefinite plural آلهة lacks the universal scope required for exception.
rows.anchor: والجمع إذا كان نكرة لم يستثن منه عند جماعة من المحققين

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad allows apposition because لو is semantically non-affirmative, making apposition preferable to adjectival description.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أبو العباس المبرد في إلا الله أن يكون بدلا

rows.speaker: أبو علي الشلوبين
rows.claim: Al-Shulubīn analyzes إلا as غير in the sense of “in place of”: a man other than Zayd means a man replacing Zayd.
rows.anchor: فإلا بمعنى غير التي بمعنى مكان

rows.speaker: ابن الصائغ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sa’igh says the sense is sound only if إلا means غير as a substitute for the one God, following Sibawayh’s example.
rows.anchor: لا يصح المعنى عندي إلا أن تكون إلا في معنى غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proving divine unity, the text exalts God as owner of all creation and of perfect power and judgment; His acts cannot be challenged because they are wholly wise.
rows.anchor: إذ له أن يفعل في ملكه ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of لا يسأل is universal in time; the verb يفعل encompasses all divine acts, including creation, provision, benefit, and harm.
rows.anchor: والظاهر في قوله لا يسئل العموم في الأزمان

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj restricts the questioning to the Resurrection: God is not questioned about His judgment of servants, while they are questioned about their deeds.
rows.anchor: أي في القيامة لا يسئل عن حكمه في عباده

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr explains that God is not brought to account, whereas people are; another reported view says He is not punished while they are.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: لا يحاسب وهم يحاسبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are questioned because they are owned servants who often err and deserve to be asked why they acted as they did.
rows.anchor: لأنهم مملوكون مستعبدون واقع منهم الخطأ كثيرا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reads لا يسل and يسئلون with a light fatha on the sīn, transferring the hamza’s vowel and deleting it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: لا يسل ويسلون بفتح السين نقل حركة الهمزة إلى السين وحذف الهمزة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The renewed question about taking gods besides God intensifies the indictment, especially by stressing that they deliberately chose to reject Him.
rows.anchor: استفظاعا لشأنهم واستعظاما لكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No rational or transmitted proof supports partners for God; prior scriptures and the revelation brought by Muhammad testify to divine uniqueness.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة تقوم على أن الله تعالى شريكا لا من جهة العقل ولا من جهة النقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This is a reminder for those with me and before me” can mean scripture for Muhammad’s community and earlier prophetic communities.
rows.anchor: هذا ذكر من معي أي عظة للذين معي وهم أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “this” points to the Qur’an: it reminds later people through its call and law and earlier people through their histories and reports of the unseen.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا إشارة إلى القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Qur’an interpretation, the invitation to produce proof presents the Qur’an itself as the demonstrative argument.
rows.anchor: عرض القرآن في معرض البرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read ذكر annexed to من, with the verbal noun governing its object; other readings use tanwīn and treat من as its object.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بإضافة ذكر إلى من فيهما على إضافة المصدر إلى المفعول

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Ya‘mar and Talha read ذكر with tanwīn and break the mīm of معي, taking مع as a companion noun governed by من; Abu Hatim rejects the construction as unsupported.
rows.anchor: وضعف أبو حاتم هذه القراءة لدخول من على مع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talha and other transmitters also vary whether ذكر is tanwīn or annexed and whether من قبلي has a broken mīm.
rows.anchor: وعن طلحة ذكر منونا معي دون من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read الحق in the accusative as the object of يعلمون; their ignorance of truth is the root of their corruption and failure to distinguish truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: والظاهر نصبه على المفعول به فلا يعلمون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows accusative الحق to emphasize the preceding proposition: they do not know the truth, not falsehood.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المنصوب أيضا على معنى التوكيد لمضمون الجملة السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is that ignorance causes their turning away; Ibn Atiyya reverses the relation, saying they turn away and therefore do not know truth.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الإعراض متسبب عن انتفاء العلم

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says their turning away is the reason they do not know truth, rather than their ignorance causing the turning away.
rows.anchor: وليس المعنى فهم معرضون لأنهم لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan, Humayd, and Ibn Muhaysin read الحق in the nominative, either as a predicate with an omitted subject or a subject with an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وحميد وابن محيصن الحق بالرفع

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: On the nominative reading, Ibn Atiyya takes the phrase to say “this statement is the truth” and pauses after لا يعلمون.
rows.anchor: هذا القول هو الحق والوقف على هذه القراءة على لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari construes the nominative as emphatic placement between cause and result: their ignorance-driven turning away is the truth, not falsehood.
rows.anchor: إعراضهم بسبب الجهل هو الحق لا الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every messenger taught that God alone is deity and commanded worship; revelation agrees on this creed though legal rulings differ.
rows.anchor: هذه العقيدة من توحيد الله لم تختلف فيها النبوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic singular “a messenger” takes a singular verb but a plural command, which may address the messenger’s community as well as him.
rows.anchor: أفرد على اللفظ في قوله إلا يوحى إليه ثم جمع على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group of readers, including the two Hamzas and al-A‘mash, read نوحي with the divine first-person plural; most of the Seven read يوحى, and ‘Asim varies.
rows.anchor: واختلف عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse may have been revealed about Khuza‘a’s claim that angels are God’s daughters, with similar claims about Jesus by Christians and Ezra by Jews.
rows.anchor: ونزلت في خزاعة حيث قالوا: الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عباد مكرمون can include angels, Ezra, and Christ; al-Zamakhshari takes it specifically of angels, whose servitude rules out divine offspring.
rows.anchor: ويشمل هذا اللفظ الملائكة وعزيرا والمسيح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the angels’ honored closeness misled some people into claiming they were God’s children, although their servitude refutes this.
rows.anchor: والعبودية تنافي الولادة إلا أنهم مكرمون مقربون عندي

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads مكرمون with gemination; the majority read it without gemination.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة مكرمون بالتشديد والجمهور بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase لا يسبقونه means the angels follow God’s speech and do not speak before He does; one reading has kasra, another ḍamma on the bā’ from the verb “to outstrip.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ لا يسبقونه بكسر الباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In بالقول, Kufans take the definite article as replacing a possessive pronoun, while Basrans posit an omitted pronoun meaning “their speech.”
rows.anchor: وأل في بالقول نابت مناب الضمير على مذهب الكوفيين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari likewise explains بالقول as their speech, with the article standing in place of annexation or an omitted pronoun.
rows.anchor: والمراد بقولهم فأنيبت اللام مناب الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the angels’ words follow God’s, their deeds are also governed by His command; they perform no act until commanded.
rows.anchor: فكما أن قولهم تابع لقوله كذلك فعلهم مبني على أمره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets what is before and behind the angels as their past and future deeds.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعلم ما قدموا وما أخروا من أعمالهم

rows.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
rows.claim: Ammar ibn Yasir explains the phrase as what the angels have done and what they have yet to do.
rows.anchor: وقال نحوه عمار بن ياسر، قال: ما عملوا وما لم يعملوا بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations reverse the temporal framing, taking before them as the Hereafter and behind them as this world, or the reverse, or as all time before and after creation.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما بين أيديهم الآخرة وما خلفهم الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels intercede only for those God approves as worthy of increased reward and honor, and remain apprehensive of God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: وأهله للشفاعة في زيادة الثواب والتعظيم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the approved person is one who professes “There is no god but God,” and the angels’ intercession is asking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لمن ارتضى هو من قال: لا إله إلا الله وشفاعتهم: الاستغفار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes the approved person as anyone God deems worthy of intercession.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لمن ارتضاه الله أن يشفع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view limits angelic intercession to the Resurrection, while an authentic report says they intercede in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيح أنهم يشفعون في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that a self-proclaimed angelic deity would enter Hell is hypothetical and illustrative, magnifying shirk and the importance of monotheism.
rows.anchor: على سبيل العرض والتمثيل مع علمه بأنه لا يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy to “if they had associated partners” serves to make shirk’s enormity clear; the condition can govern either possible or impossible cases.
rows.anchor: قصد بذلك تفظيع أمر الشرك وتعظيم شأن التوحيد

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن المقري
rows.claim: The majority read نجزيه with an open nūn; Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri reads it as نجزئه from أجزأ, “suffice,” with hamza lightened to yā’.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن المقري بضمها أراد نجزئه بالهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الظالمين here means disbelievers who put things in the wrong place.
rows.anchor: وهم الكافرون والواضعون الشيء في غير موضعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Ata, al-Dahhak, and Qatada say heaven and earth were one mass, then God separated them by air.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن وعطاء والضحاك وقتادة: كانتا شيئا واحدا ففصل الله بينهما بالهواء.

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka‘b says the heavens and earth were layered, then a wind was made between them and split them into seven heavens and seven earths.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: خلق الله السموات والأرض بعضها على بعض ثم خلق ريحا بوسطها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Abu Salih say heaven and earth were a single joined layer, split into seven heavens and seven earths.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والسدي وأبو صالح: كانت السموات والأرض مؤتلفة طبقة واحدة ففتقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views say they were joined by darkness and separated by light, or that sky before rain and earth before plants were joined and split by rain and growth.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: السماء قبل المطر رتق، والأرض قبل النبات رتق

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the rain-and-growth interpretation because it combines a lesson, a counted blessing, and visible proof, fitting the statement that all life is from water.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول حسن يجمع العبرة وتعديد النعمة والحجة للمحسوس بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under physical separation theories “see” means eyesight; under the other accounts it means intellectual recognition. The Qur’anic miracle makes the claim almost directly witnessed, and separation needs a determining cause.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذين القولين تكون الرؤية من البصر وعلى ما قبلهما من رؤية القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read رتقا with a still tā’ as a verbal noun used adjectivally and as predicate of the dual subject; Hasan and others read a fatha, a noun meaning something closed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور رتقا بسكون التاء وهو مصدر يوصف به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the fatha reading by supplying an omitted noun: the pair were “a thing that was joined.”
rows.anchor: هو على تقدير موصوف أي كانتا شيئا رتقا

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
rows.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi says both forms can be verbal nouns, but the fatha usually suggests a passive noun; here both function as predicates without dual inflection, like رجل عدل and رجلين عدل.
rows.anchor: لكن هنا الأولى أن يكونا مصدرين فأقيم كل واحد منهما مقام المفعولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If جعلنا takes one object, “every living thing from water” means every animal is made from water, its material being semen; Qutrub and others hold this view.
rows.anchor: أي مادته النطفة قاله قطرب وجماعة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and others say living things are described as created from water because water sustains them and they cannot endure without it; life is literal, with angels and jinn excepted.
rows.anchor: وكان محتاجا إليه لا يصبر عنه جعل مخلوقا منه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes “every living thing” to include all growing things, plants and minerals; life is metaphorical or means the shared feature of growth, and the scope remains qualified.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: أي خلقنا كل نام من الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If جعلنا takes two objects, God made every thing living through some water on which it depends.
rows.anchor: وإن تعدت جعلنا لاثنين فالمعنى صيرنا كل شيء حي بسبب من الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read حي in the genitive as an adjective of شيء; Humayd reads حيا in the accusative as جعلنا’s second object.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حميد حيا بالنصب مفعولا ثانيا لجعلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question أفلا يؤمنون rebukes their weak reasoning and urges reflection on these proofs and abandonment of idolatry; the verse gives heavenly and earthly signs of unity.
rows.anchor: أفلا يتدبرون هذه الأدلة ويعملوا بمقتضاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stable mountains and pathways in the earth continue the sequence of earthly proofs; the pronoun فيها apparently refers to earth, though it may refer to the mountains.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في فيها عائد على الأرض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats فجاجا as an adjective moved before سبل, making it a circumstantial phrase: the land was created with broad roads, whereas the other verse simply describes roads.
rows.anchor: وهي يعني فجاجا صفة ولكن جعلت حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A descriptive modifier need not characterize its noun at the time of speaking, unlike a circumstantial phrase; thus the different word order carries a different implication.
rows.anchor: فلو تأخر فجاجا لكان صفة كما في تلك الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything raised and arched over something is called a roof; the sky is preserved in several possible senses.
rows.anchor: وما رفع وسمك على شيء فهو سقف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the sky is protected from decay and change through the long passage of time.
rows.anchor: حفظ من البلى والتغير على طول الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are that the sky is prevented from falling without support, protected from shirk and sin, or protected from devils by shooting stars.
rows.anchor: حفظ من السقوط لإمساكه من غير علاقة ولا عماد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits a prophetic report describing the sky as a raised roof and restrained wave, moving like an arrow and protected from devils; if sound, it directly explains the verse.
rows.anchor: إن السماء سقف مرفوع وموج مكفوف يجري كما يجري السهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s signs include the sun, moon, stars, their courses and timed rising and setting, all displaying wisdom and power.
rows.anchor: ما وضع الله فيها من الأدلة والعبر بالشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read آياتها in the plural; Mujahid and Humayd read a singular, referring either to the whole created sky as one sign or to a generic collective.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد عن آيتها بالإفراد

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says people notice worldly benefits from the sky—light, navigation, and rain sustaining life—but ignore its clear evidence of a Creator.
rows.anchor: هم يتفطنون لما يرد عليهم من السماء من المنافع الدنياوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In كل يسبحون the nunation compensates for an omitted annexed noun; فلك is the circular body or course of day and night.
rows.anchor: والتنوين في كل عوض من المضاف إليه، والفلك الجسم الدائر دورة اليوم والليلة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi explain الفلك as the sky.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس والسدي: الفلك السماء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators call الفلك a contained wave beneath the sky; Qatada describes it as a circular orbit between heaven and earth while the sky stays fixed.
rows.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين: الفلك موج مكفوف تحت السماء تجري فيه الشمس والقمر.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Other reports identify the orbit as the pole, an orbit particular to each planet, or an immaterial track; al-Dahhak says it is not a body.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: الفلك ليس بجسم وإنما هو مدار هذه النجوم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent view is that the orbit is a body and every celestial object swims in one orbit; another view assigns each its own.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه جسم وفيه الاختلاف المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural verb يسبحون may imply an omitted coordinated “stars”; without an omitted plural, the verb would be dual.
rows.anchor: فقيل ثم معطوف محذوف وهو والنجوم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes the pronoun refer to the sun and moon as recurring classes of risings, metaphorically pluralized despite each being one.
rows.anchor: جعلوها متكاثرة لتكاثر مطالعها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra’ says the masculine intelligent plural is used because swimming is an action associated with people; al-Razi reports Ibn Sina’s view that the bodies themselves reason.
rows.anchor: لما كانت السباحة من أفعال الآدميين جاء ما أسند إليهما مجموعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may be independent or circumstantial of sun and moon; night and day cannot be the objects moving in an orbit, which itself does not move.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل عليه الظاهر أن الشمس والقمر هما اللذان يجريان في الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was said to answer Muslims who thought Muhammad immortal, or disbelievers who objected that a human messenger eats and dies.
rows.anchor: وقيل: طعن كفار مكة عليه بأنه بشر يأكل الطعام ويموت

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the disbelievers expected Muhammad to die and hoped to gloat; no human is immortal, so his opponents will also die.
rows.anchor: فلا أنت ولا هم إلا عرضة للموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem attributed to al-Shafi‘i and another verse reinforce that death is a shared path and mockers will meet the same fate.
rows.anchor: تمنى رجال أن أموت وإن أمت

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and Muqatil report that Abu Jahl called Muhammad a prophet of Abd Manaf; Abu Sufyan defended that lineage, and the Prophet rebuked Abu Jahl and called Abu Sufyan’s answer tribal pride.
rows.anchor: قال السدي ومقاتل: مر الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام بأبي جهل وأبي سفيان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers mock the Prophet in retaliation because criticism of their gods pains them; إن is a negation equivalent to ما.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الكفار يغمهم ذكر آلهتهم بسوء شرعوا في الاستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent جواب of إذا is إن يتخذونك; its use with a negative without ف, like a negative ما clause, supports treating إذا as governed by the following verb rather than the response.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن جواب إذا هو إن يتخذونك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative supplies an omitted “they say” as جواب إذا, with إن يتخذونك إلا هزوا parenthetical; the phrase means they take the Prophet as an object of ridicule.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جواب إذا محذوف وهو يقولون المحكي به قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يذكر may mean praise or blame, but context makes their question mean that Muhammad speaks ill of their gods; هزوا is the second object of يتخذونك.
rows.anchor: والذكر يكون بالخير وبالشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mocking is hypocritical because they themselves disbelieve in the Merciful’s reminder, meaning the Qur’an; the clause is apparently circumstantial to their quoted speech.
rows.anchor: وهم بذكر الرحمن هم كافرون أي ينكرون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes “they disbelieve in the mention of the Merciful” a circumstantial clause explaining that disbelief is the basis of their ridicule.
rows.anchor: والجملة في موضع الحال أي يتخذونك هزوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the verse followed their denial of the name الرحمن: they claimed to know it only as a name at al-Yamama; here it means God.
rows.anchor: وروي أنها نزلت حين أنكروا لفظة الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they hasten to demand punishment, God first rebukes humanity’s excessive haste; الإنسان is the human species, figuratively described as made of haste because this behavior recurs.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه يراد بالإنسان هنا اسم الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The figurative reading makes sense of the command to wait for God’s signs, namely the threatened punishment; a person is called “of” a habit he repeatedly displays.
rows.anchor: وبهذا التأويل يتم معنى الآية ويترتب عليه قوله سأريكم آياتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Amr’s inverted reading and Ibn Mas‘ud’s wording mean that haste was made part of human nature; Abu Hayyan rejects the inversion as unsuitable to eloquent prose outside poetry.
rows.anchor: فليس قوله بجيد لأن القلب الصحيح فيه أن لا يكون في كلام فصيح

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and several early authorities identify the human as Adam; Mujahid says his soul reached his head and eyes, he saw sunset, and asked God to finish creating him before it set.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: لما دخل الروح رأسه وعينيه رأى الشمس قاربت الغروب

rows.speaker: سعيد
rows.claim: Sa‘id says Adam nearly stood when the soul reached his knees, prompting the description of the human as created in haste.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد: لما بلغت الروح ركبتيه كاد يقوم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says God created Adam on Friday, completing his creation in haste.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: خلقه الله يوم الجمعة على عجلة في خلقه.

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash derives haste from God’s command كن, which immediately brought Adam into being.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش من عجل لأن الله قال له كن فكان.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets haste as weakness, meaning the human is made from weak semen.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: من عجل أي ضعيف يعني النطفة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says humanity was created quickly, without the usual stages from sperm through clot and lump; Abu Hayyan traces it back to al-Akhfash.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خلق بسرعة وتعجيل على غير تريب الآدميين من النطفة والعلقة والمضغة، وهذا يرجع لقول الأخفش.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes ʿajal as clay in Himyari usage; Abu Ubayda cites a Himyari poem as evidence.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من عجل من طين والعجل بلغة حمير الطين. وأنشد أبو عبيدة لبعض الحميريين:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation quotes a line pairing the palm’s growth with water and العجل.
rows.anchor: النبع في الصخرة الصماء منبته ... والنخل منبته في الماء والعجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the human as al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, but Abu Hayyan says the species-wide reading best fits the verse’s ending.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الإنسان هنا النضر بن الحارث والذي ينبغي أن تحمل الآية عليه هو القول الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised signs may be destruction in this life and punishment in the next, proofs of monotheism and the Prophet’s truth, or traces of past peoples; the first reading is preferred, including Badr.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أليق أي سيأتي ما يسوؤكم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari answers the apparent conflict between created haste and a command not to hurry: people can restrain implanted desire because God gives them that capacity; Abu Hayyan notes the Mu‘tazilite basis.
rows.anchor: لأنه أعطاه القدرة التي يستطيع بها قمع الشهوة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Humayd, and Ibn Muqsim read خلق actively, with God as subject and الإنسان as object.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وابن مقسم خلق مبنيا للفاعل الإنسان بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متى هذا الوعد is a mocking question; the Muslims had threatened the disbelievers with punishment through revelation.
rows.anchor: استفهام على جهة الهزء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: متى is apparently genitive after هذا; some Kufans instead treat it as an adverb governed by an implied يكون or يجيء.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن بعض الكوفيين أن موضع متى نصب على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The result of لو is omitted for emphasis; proposed completions include that they would hurry to believe or know the Resurrection and promised event are real.
rows.anchor: وجواب لو محذوف لدلالة الكلام عليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari construes حين as the object of يعلم, or leaves يعلم intransitive and links حين to an implied “when”; at that time they will realize their error.
rows.anchor: وحين منصوب بمضمر أي حين لا يكفون عن وجوههم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan’s apparent reading supplies the omitted object of يعلم from context: they would know the arrival of the promise they mockingly demanded.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أن مفعول يعلم محذوف لدلالة ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حين can be attached to the understood arrival of the promise; the passage describes people directly facing fire and unable to protect their faces.
rows.anchor: والمعنى لو يعلمون مباشرة النار حين لا يكفونها عن وجوههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faces are singled out as the noblest part, containing the senses and the part people most instinctively protect; the following mention of backs generalizes to the whole body.
rows.anchor: وذكر الوجوه لأنها أشرف ما في الإنسان وعجل حواسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says بل introduces an implied contrast: the signs will not arrive on the terms the disbelievers propose, but punishment will strike them suddenly.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية بل تأتيهم استدراك مقدر قبله نفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in تأتيهم apparently refers to the fire; other views refer it to the Hour, punishment, the promise, the appointed time, or resurrection.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في تأتيهم عائد على النار

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-A‘mash reads بل يأتيهم and يبهتهم with masculine verbs and فتح on غ, referring back to the promise or appointed time.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش بل يأتيهم بالياء بغتة بفتح الغين

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
rows.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi suggests the masculine may refer to fire understood as punishment, after which the reading returns to the word’s feminine form.
rows.anchor: لعله جعل النار بمعنى العذاب فذكر ثم رد ردها إلى ظاهر اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا هم ينظرون means they will not be given a delay or respite.
rows.anchor: أي يؤخرون عما حل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were mocked too, and their mockers reaped destruction and punishment in both worlds; the passage recalls the parallel in al-An‘am.
rows.anchor: وتقدم تفسير مثل هذه الآية في الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks who guards people by night and day from God’s might; it is a rebuke with the answer omitted: no protector exists.
rows.anchor: وفي آخر الكلام تقدير محذوف كأنه ليس لهم مانع ولا كالىء،

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya connects بل to the statement that they turn away from remembering their Lord: they do not identify any guardian.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا النفي تركيب بل في قوله بل هم عن ذكر ربهم معرضون

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says they are unfit to answer who guards them, since they do not remember God or fear His power even while He protects them.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنه أمر رسوله بسؤالهم عن الكالئ ثم بين أنهم لا يصلحون لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far, al-Zuhri, and Shayba read يكلوكم with a light ḍamma and no hamza; al-Kisa’i and al-Farra’ transmit a form with fatḥa on lām and a still wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر والزهري وشيبة: يكلوكم بضمة خفيفة من غير همز.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent interpretation of shrinking earth is that God reduces disbelieving lands by letting Muslims conquer them and turn them into Muslim territory.
rows.anchor: نقص أرض الكفر ودار الحرب ونحذف أطرافها بتسليط المسلمين عليها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says mentioning that God comes to the land vividly depicts Muslim armies and detachments arriving victorious and reducing enemy territory; this encourages believers.
rows.anchor: تصوير ما كان الله يجريه على أيدي المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators say the verse was revealed about Meccan disbelievers; its question whether they are victorious is a rebuke for failing to notice their losses.
rows.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أنها نزلت في كفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet warns by revelation, not personal invention; divine warnings must come true, as the visible shrinking of enemy territory already shows.
rows.anchor: إنما أنذركم بالوحي أي أعلمكم بما تخافون منه بوحي من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warned are called deaf because revelation is heard: they block their ears and gain nothing from warning; the definite noun emphasizes their deliberate deafness.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الوحي من المسموعات كان ذكر الصمم مناسبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority read يسمع with the deaf as subject and الدعاء as object; other readings make the Prophet the subject, either active or passive, or make the warning itself the subject by extension.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور يسمع بفتح الياء والميم الصم رفع به والدعاء نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a slight touch of punishment makes them cry out and confess their earlier injustice and disbelief.
rows.anchor: نادوا بالهلاك وأقروا بأنهم كانوا ظالمين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains نفحة as a slight breeze or touch; another report from him identifies it as the famine that struck Mecca.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نفحة طرف وعنه هو الجوع الذي نزل بمكة.

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj takes نفحة as a small share, based on the phrase for giving someone a little portion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: نصيب من قولهم نفح له من العطاء نفحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three features emphasize how little punishment suffices: the word “touch,” the slightness of نفح, and its one-time form; the smallest exposure makes them submit.
rows.anchor: ثلاث مبالغات لفظ المس، وما في مدلول النفح من القلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scales of the Resurrection express perfect divine justice; the interpretation of scales as literal instruments is the majority view.
rows.anchor: واختلاف الناس في ذلك هل ثم ميزان حقيقة وهو قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Qatada say there is no physical scale; the expression represents complete justice, with القسط used as an emphatic adjective.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الضحاك وقتادة؟ قالا: ليس ثم ميزان ولكنه العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other grammatical possibilities make الموازين possessors of justice by ellipsis, or take القسط as the purpose for which they are set up.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا لأجله أي لأجل القسط

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the lām in ليوم as indicating the time something is due; he supports the construction with a line from al-Nabigha.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: مثلها في قولك: جئت لخمس ليال خلون من الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufan grammarians, Ibn Qutayba, and Ibn Malik allow the lām to mean “in”; another view makes it causal with an omitted noun, for the accounting of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وذهب الكوفيون إلى أن اللام تكون بمعنى في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has القسط with ṣād instead of sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء القصط بالصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read مثقال in the accusative as the predicate of كان with an omitted “thing” or “deed”; Zayd ibn Ali and others read it nominative as subject of a complete كان.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: مثقال بالنصب خبر كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most read أتينا from “come/bring”; Ubayy’s جئنا clarifies this. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others read آتينا from reciprocal recompense, so it takes ب.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وابن أبي إسحاق

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
rows.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi says the long-vowel reading means requiting, not “giving” from آتى, since the latter would not govern the preposition ب.
rows.anchor: ولو كان على أفعلنا من الإيتاء بالمد على ما توهمه بعضهم لتعدى مطلقا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the reciprocal sense: people bring deeds and God brings their recompense.
rows.anchor: لأنهم أتوه بالأعمال وأتاهم بالجزاء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya likewise derives the reading from mutual recompense and says replacing initial wāw with hamza is not a familiar Arabic pattern.
rows.anchor: ويوهن هذه القراءة أن بدل الواو المفتوحة همزة ليس بمعروف

rows.speaker: حميد
rows.claim: Humayd reads أثبنا بها from reward; the feminine pronoun refers to a mustard seed through its feminine head noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حميد: أثبنا بها من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We suffice as reckoners” assures that every deed is counted and none is absent; ḥisāb means enumeration, though another view takes it as recompense.
rows.anchor: وهو إشارة إلى ضبط أعمالهم من الحساب وهو العد والإحصاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of the Qur’an and its opponents is followed by the precedent of Moses and Aaron, given the Furqan, light, and reminder, before the text returns to the blessed Qur’anic reminder.
rows.anchor: أتبعه بأنه عادة الله في أنبيائه فذكر ما آتى موسى وهارون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Furqan is the Torah, also called light and reminder; Ibn Abbas reads “light and reminder” without conjunction, and others explain reminder as admonition, needed guidance, or distinction and honor.
rows.anchor: والفرقان التوراة وهو الضياء، والذكر أي كتابا هو فرقان وضياء، وذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations take the Furqan as victory, as in “the Day of Furqan,” the parting of the sea, or a way out of doubts; الذين may be adjectival, parenthetic, or appositional.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس الفرقان الفتح لقوله يوم الفرقان

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most say the God-fearing fear Him though unseen; Muqatil specifies His punishment. Al-Zajjaj says they fear Him when no one sees them, which Ibn Atiyya prefers; Abu Sulayman says they fear Him when out of people’s sight.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يخافونه من حيث لا يراهم أحد ورجحه ابن عطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإشفاق is intense fear; the statement about fearing the Hour may stand independently or join the relative clause, contrasting an ongoing worldly state with a fixed afterlife trait.
rows.anchor: والإشفاق شدة الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a blessed reminder, abundant in benefit and rich in news; the text puts a noun adjective before a descriptive clause in the usual order.
rows.anchor: وهذا أي القرآن ذكر مبارك أي كثير منافعه غزير خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuking question addresses disbelievers; له refers to the Qur’an and comforts the Prophet by recalling that earlier peoples also rejected revelation given to Moses.
rows.anchor: والضمير في له عائد على ذكر وهو القرآن

none: The segment contains only the Qur’anic text of 26:150–189, with no commentary or distinct source claims.
